Let $\vec{a}, \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}$ and $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{a} \times \vec{c}, \vec{a}
eq 0$. Show that $\vec{b}=\vec{c}$.
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot(\vec{b}-\vec{c})=0$
⇒ either $\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{b}}=\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{c}}$ or $\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{a}} \perp(\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{b}}-\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{c}})$, since $\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{a}}
eq 0$
Also, $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{a} \times \vec{c} \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times(\vec{b}-\vec{c})=0$
⇒ either $\vec{b}=\vec{c}$ or $\vec{a} \|(\vec{b}-\vec{c})$, since $\vec{a}
eq 0$
Since vectors $\vec{a}$ and $(\vec{b}-\vec{c})$ cannot be $\|$ and $\perp$ simultaneously
Hence $\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{b}}=\overrightarrow{\boldsymbol{c}}$

questions.q:
Three friends A, B and C move out from the same location O at the same time in three different directions to reach their destinations. They move out on straight paths and decide that A and B after reaching their destinations will meet up with $C$ at his predecided destination, following straight paths from $A$ to $C$ and $B$ to $C$ in such a way that $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}$, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OB}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OC}}=5 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}}$ respectively.

Based upon the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Complete the given figure to explain their entire movement plan along the respective vectors.
(ii) Find vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}}$.
(iii) (a) If $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=1$, distance of O to A is 1 km and that from O to B is 2 km, then find the angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OA}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OB}}$. Also, find $|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$.
(iii) (b) If $\vec{a}=2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, then find a unit vector perpendicular to $(\vec{a}+\vec{b})$ and $(\vec{a}-\vec{b})$.

questions.q:
An instructor at the astronomical centre shows three among the brightest stars in a particular constellation. Assume that the telescope is located at $\mathrm{O}(0,0,0)$ and the three stars have their locations at the points $\mathrm{D}, \mathrm{A}$ and V having position vectors $2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}, 7 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}$ and $-3 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}+11 \hat{k}$ respectively.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) How far is the star V from star A ?
(ii) Find a unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{DA}}$.
(iii) Find the measure of $\angle \mathrm{VDA}$.
(iii)(b) What is the projection of vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{DV}}$ on vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{DA}}$ ?
questions.solution:
(i) $\overrightarrow{A V}=$ Position Vector of $\mathrm{V}-$ Position Vector of A
$=-3 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}+11 \hat{k}-7 \hat{i}-5 \hat{j}-8 \hat{k}=-10 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$
Thus, $|\overrightarrow{A V}|=\sqrt{100+4+9}=\sqrt{113}$ units
(ii) $\overrightarrow{D A}=$ Position Vector of $\mathrm{A}-$ Position Vector of D
$=7 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}-2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}-4 \hat{k}=5 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}$
Unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{D A}=\frac{5 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}}{3 \sqrt{5}}$
(iii) $\overrightarrow{D V}=-5 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}$
$\angle V D A=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{D V} \cdot \overrightarrow{D A}}{|\overrightarrow{D V}||\overrightarrow{D A}|}\right)=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{11 \sqrt{2}}{90}\right)$
(iii) (b)
(iii) $\overrightarrow{D V}=-5 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}$
Projection of $\overrightarrow{D V}$ on $\overrightarrow{D A}=\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{D V} \cdot \overrightarrow{D A}}{|\overrightarrow{D A}|}\right)=\frac{11 \sqrt{5}}{15}$

questions.solution: Diagonal vectors are: $\vec{a}+\vec{b}=3 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}=-\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}$ (or, $\vec{b}-\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-8 \hat{k}$ )] $\therefore$ unit vectors are $\frac{(\vec{a}+\vec{b})}{|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|}=\frac{3}{7} \hat{i}+\frac{6}{7} \hat{j}-\frac{2}{7} \hat{k}$ and $\frac{(\vec{a}-\vec{b})}{|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{69}} \hat{i}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{69}} \hat{j}+\frac{8}{\sqrt{69}} \hat{k}$
